clue.text: Disciplined soldier

blocks.note: first meaning: neat, well organised, behaving in a controlled way
second meaning: a soldier who attends an officer or works in a military hospital

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a well-drilled soldier, but the adjective and the noun are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for tidy, controlled behaviour and also a noun for an army attendant or hospital porter.

clue.text: RU action, with parts exchanged, laid back

indicators.note: swapping the two parts of a compound moves its back half to the front, a rotation of its letters

blocks.note: RU is Rugby Union, and a hand-off is the move of pushing a tackler away with an open hand

explanation.surface: Something done in a rugby match, with its stages switched round, is described as relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: HAND-OFF with its halves swapped gives OFFHAND. RU is the standard abbreviation for Rugby Union.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual and unconcerned, which is the sense of relaxed and easygoing in the phrase.

clue.text: Rigid Metal Co. put out calculating machine

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or displaced, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm called Rigid Metal Company has released a new calculating device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as a phrase meaning released, but 'put' is fodder and only 'out' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer working on digital data is an electronic device for performing calculations, hence a calculating machine.

clue.text: Reserve strange rite with feeling, they say

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put into an unusual order
what people say is heard rather than seen, so the preceding word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a sense is a feeling, spelt here to match the ending needed

explanation.surface: A restrained manner is described as an odd ceremony performed with emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a noun means a quiet, restrained manner, a tendency to hold back one's thoughts, which is reticence.

clue.text: Rising TV company holding number for a long time

indicators.note: holding means gripping something within, so one piece sits inside the other
in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster
NO is the usual abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A broadcaster on the up has held on to one number for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first and the whole thing then reads upwards. Yonks is British slang for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is informal British slang meaning ages, an extremely lengthy period, as in not seeing someone for yonks.

clue.text: Being distressed, fitted with warning device

blocks.note: first meaning: frightened or anxious
second meaning: equipped with a burglar alarm or similar

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves read like a nervous homeowner; they are two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone frightened or worried, and also a building or car that has a security system installed.

clue.text: Somewhat restrained, bats ten in order

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them afresh, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cautious cricketer bats tenth in the batting order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order' looks like one phrase, but 'in' belongs to the fodder and 'order' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abstinent holds back from indulgence such as drink, so they are self-denying and moderate in their habits.

clue.text: Unique shellfish sailor discarded

indicators.note: something discarded is thrown away, so those letters drop out of the larger word

blocks.note: an abalone is an edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell
AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind shellfish is thrown away by a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alone in its class has no equal or companion, so it is the only one of its kind.

clue.text: A reduction in manufacturing?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cutback in factory output
setter's reading: making things smaller, as in shrinking electronic components

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like an economic downturn; the reduction is in the size of the things made.
explanation.definitionFit: The process of designing and building ever smaller versions of devices is a reduction carried out in production.

clue.text: Showed contempt of document about travel, mainly

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so the word loses its last letter
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a deed is a legal document
to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone scorned the paperwork concerning a journey, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule, treating something with scorn, so the past tense means mocked scornfully.

clue.text: Confers one right in order to stand up for oneself

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them afresh, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grants a person a right so they can defend themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight one's corner is an idiom from boxing meaning to argue or defend one's own position or interests.

clue.text: Top place in classical Greek

blocks.note: first meaning: a room just under the roof of a house
second meaning: the dialect of ancient Athens, the main form of classical Greek

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a phrase about Greek, but it holds two meanings joined by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the uppermost room of a house; Attic, from Attica around Athens, names the literary dialect of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Blow the eccentric employed at the checkout

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun

blocks.note: a swipe is a sweeping blow
a card is an amusing or odd person

explanation.surface: An odd person working on the till takes a swing at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling someone 'a card' means they are a joker or character.
explanation.definitionFit: A swipe card is a plastic card passed through a reader, used for payment or entry, as at a shop till.

clue.text: Outline of ale tin thrown in river

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed about, so these letters land in a new order
in places one group inside another

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the Wales–England border
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A beer can tossed into a river leaves a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to describe or draw the outline of something, marking out its edges precisely.

clue.text: Record replacing note in Anthony Palgrave's work

indicators.note: replacing means one thing takes another's place within the word

blocks.note: a log is a written record
N, for note, as in banknote
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recording takes over a passage in the writings of someone named Anthony Palgrave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anthony Palgrave' looks like one name, but Palgrave is the definition. Francis Turner Palgrave compiled The Golden Treasury of English poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Palgrave's Golden Treasury is a famous collection of poems by various writers, which is an anthology.

clue.text: Establish cast

blocks.note: first meaning: to set up an institution
second meaning: to shape molten metal in a mould

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests a theatre company, but both words are verbs with separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To found is to set up a company or college, and also to melt and mould metal, as in a foundry.

clue.text: Possibly wrote flop - one containing bloomers?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be rearranged into something else

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An author wrote a failure, a book full of blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers look like blunders or underwear; here they are things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot for plants holds blooming plants, and bloomer is a playful word for something that blooms.

clue.text: The worker leaves the animal to run away

indicators.note: leaves means departs from, so those letters go out of the larger word

blocks.note: an antelope is a deer-like grazing animal
the worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: A farmhand abandons the livestock to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to flee secretly, usually to marry, so it means to escape or bolt.

clue.text: Finish endless war cry and make entrance

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: the end is the finish
a chant is a slogan shouted by a crowd

explanation.surface: A warrior ends a battle cry and walks onstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as an arrival, but it is the verb en-TRANCE, to put into a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or bewitch them, which is exactly what to enchant means.

clue.text: One making his mark at the Edinburgh Festival?

definitions.text: One making his mark at the Edinburgh Festival?

blocks.clueFragment: One making his mark at the Edinburgh Festival?
blocks.note: surface reading: a performer who makes a name for themselves at the arts festival
setter's reading: someone inking marks on skin, linked to the Edinburgh Military Tattoo

explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Military Tattoo is a famous military show at the castle each August; a tattoo is also an inked design.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who inks designs into skin literally makes marks, and the word tattoo also names the Edinburgh show.

clue.text: Worries - with three missing locks

indicators.note: three missing means a trio of letters is dropped from the front of the word

blocks.note: to distress someone is to worry them

explanation.surface: Anxieties lead to three strands of hair falling out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tresses are long locks of a person's hair, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Account has debts following agricultural policy that's generous

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the account and debts are placed behind the policy

blocks.note: CAP is the EU's Common Agricultural Policy
AC is the abbreviation for account
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: Farm subsidies with accounts and debts are described as lavish.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous can mean large or ample in size, as in generous portions, matching roomy, spacious capacious.

clue.text: Vehicle with the French guy

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A man arrives in a taxi with a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' reads as a man, but it is a guy rope, a supporting line.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a rope or wire used to steady a tent or mast, and a strong rope or wire is a cable.

clue.text: Fish, Jack?

blocks.note: first meaning: a small herring-like sea fish
second meaning: the surname of Jack in the nursery rhyme who could eat no fat

explanation.walkthrough: Jack is also a fish, which is the trap; the question mark points to Jack Sprat of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small edible sea fish, and Jack Sprat is the lean husband in the traditional rhyme.

clue.text: Get rid of most of spots in middle of week

indicators.note: most of means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
the middle of a word is its central letters, which are the ones kept
in places one group inside another

blocks.note: the two central letters of the word
a rash is an outbreak of spots

explanation.surface: Someone tries to clear up their acne by midweek.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete, so it means to remove or eliminate something completely.

clue.text: Personal accounts?

blocks.note: surface reading: private bank accounts
setter's reading: written stories of one's own life

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like banking; the accounts are narratives, and personal means about the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Books in which people tell their own life stories are narratives of the self, very personal records.

clue.text: Some styles return, returning briefly

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters lie inside the words that follow
returning means going back, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: Fashions come back around again, put in a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' is not an indicator; its letters supply the hidden run, and 'returning' does the turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking tersely means using few words, curtly and to the point, which is what briefly means here.

clue.text: Arrangement of tunes about the army produces complaint

indicators.note: an arrangement of music is a reworking, so these letters are reordered
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A medley of military tunes leads to grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' suggests grumbling, but it is the old sense of an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint can mean a medical disorder, and tetanus is a bacterial disease causing muscle spasms.
